name: a line split at a kerning change
why: A PDF splits a line at every font and kerning change. Joined bare, the words run together and nobody can find either of them.

name: a gap the file already put in
why: One end already has whitespace, so nothing is added and the words do not come apart.

name: a gap on the leading end instead
a line break
why: The two sides disagree about which whitespace goes here - a newline against a space - and agree about everything a needle can see.

name: a footnote mark does not break the line behind it
why: A 7-unit run on a 12-unit line shifts y a little and is not a line break. It changes which whitespace lands, and not the characters.

name: an empty run between two words
why: A run that shows nothing must not be able to weld the words either side of it together.

name: a run that is only space
a hyphen gets a gap like anything else
why: A known limit rather than a decision: neither side can tell a hyphenated word broken across runs from two words, so both break it the same way and a search for cross-examination misses on both. Written down here so it is a shared limit and not a drift.
